title: Emerson as an additive LP2 running key
reader_title: Can an essay decode the beginnings of three pages?
reader_intro: Uses letter values from Ralph Waldo Emerson's essay Self-Reliance as a key, trying every starting place and checking whether the best-scoring beginning continues into the next 96 runes.

reader_test.input: The first 192 runes of LP2-00, LP2-31, and LP2-54, plus the preserved text of Emerson's Self-Reliance.
reader_test.action: Subtract Emerson's letter values, A=0 through Z=25, from rune alphabet numbers at every possible text starting place, wrapping within the 29-rune alphabet.
reader_test.check: Select the best English-pattern score on the first 96 runes, assess the next 96 at the same starting place, and compare with eight complete searches of shuffled Emerson letters.

question: Does the preserved Self-Reliance text, mapped A=0 through Z=25 and subtracted modulo 29 at any contiguous offset, produce strong 96-rune LP2 openings and held-out continuations on three fixed pages?
summary: The planted LP1 control is recovered at its exact offset. Best Emerson openings on LP2-00, 31 and 54 score near full-search shuffled-source maxima, and their continuations remain much lower than the known-reading control.

scope.representation: Preserved 50-paragraph Emerson PDF derivative normalized to 43,516 ASCII A–Z letters; A=0 through Z=25; first 192 archived rune indices of each target page; canonical GP Latin labels for scoring.
scope.procedure: For every no-wrap source offset, subtract source-letter values modulo 29 from each target's first 192 rune indices. Select the maximum English quadgram score on the first 96 runes and assess the next 96 at the same offset. Repeat the complete search on eight seeded letter shuffles. Plant a known LP1-06 reading with the same key at offset 3301 and search it blindly.
scope.parameters: LP2-00, 31 and 54; 43,325 zero-based offsets per search; 96 selection plus 96 holdout runes; eight full-source shuffles with seeds 330100–330107; one fixed source, arithmetic direction, model and representation.
scope.exclusions: Other source texts or editions, a GP segmentation of source English, reverse arithmetic, source wrapping, passage restarts, word/page-dependent key clocks, other LP2 pages or positions, non-English scoring, and any claim that running keys in general are excluded.

finding: The synthetic LP1-06 plant is ranked first and recovers exactly at offset 3301. For the three LP2 pages, Emerson's selected-window scores are within the range of eight full-search shuffled-source maxima, with low held-out scores relative to the plant. LP2-54's holdout exceeds the eight shuffled holdouts but its selected window does not, and the finite controls do not support a general significance claim.
limitations: The archived paragraph extract is a derivative of a historically linked PDF, not an authenticated creator key edition. The English quadgram scorer can reject meaningful text in other languages or representations. Eight shuffles give a comparison, not a calibrated tail probability. This tests only first-page rune windows under one fixed mapping and direction.
next_steps: Keep the top-five windows for inspection; any follow-up should specify a different source conversion or alignment before testing, preserve the complete search budget, and repeat known-reading recovery plus full-search controls and holdout evaluation.

visuals.caption: Emerson search maxima and held-out continuations against eight equally searched shuffled-source streams, with an exact planted known-reading control.

reader_finding: No convincing Emerson-key reading emerged. LP2-54’s continuation beat the eight shuffled controls, but the selected openings did not stand out and the continuations scored far below the planted reading.
reader_limit: Only the first 192 runes of LP2-00, 31 and 54 were tested, across 43,325 offsets in one extract. The rule uses A–Z values, uninterrupted subtraction and English scoring.
